questions.question: In your own words, what is simple interest and why do banks pay it?
questions.expected_answer: Simple interest is the money a bank pays you for keeping your cash with them. They pay it because they are using your money to make their own investments, so it acts like rent for your money. It is calculated only on the original amount you put in.

questions.question: If you are calculating simple interest, explain how you turn a percentage like 6,5% into a number you can put into the formula.
questions.expected_answer: You must divide the percentage by 100. So, 6,5 divided by 100 becomes 0,065. This is the decimal form you use in the P x i x n formula.

questions.question: After calculating the interest using the formula P x i x n, what must you do to find the total value of your investment?
questions.expected_answer: You must add the interest you just calculated back to the original amount (the Principal) you started with. The formula is A = P + I.
